title: Agent Finding
description: A single distilled lesson learned by an autonomous coding agent after completing a task. This is the core artifact of the agent-findings protocol: one finding per file, plain JSON, append-only. Any agent implementation that produces or consumes findings should conform to this schema so that knowledge is portable across tools and projects.

schema_version.description: Version of this protocol the finding conforms to. Consumers should tolerate unknown minor versions.

id.description: Globally unique id for the finding. Lowercase UUID v4 recommended. Doubles as the on-disk filename ({id}.json).

task_type.description: Short kebab-case category for the task this finding came from. Used as the directory shard and the primary retrieval key. Keep the vocabulary small and reusable.

language.description: Primary programming language or ecosystem of the task. Use 'none' for non-code tasks and 'multiple' when no single language dominates.

what_worked.description: The approach, technique, or insight that actually solved the problem. Written so a future agent could act on it directly. Concrete over abstract.

what_failed.description: Dead ends, wrong assumptions, or approaches that wasted time. Empty string if nothing notably failed. This is often the most valuable field — it lets other agents skip the mistake.

better_exit_condition.description: The signal that should have told the agent it was actually done (or actually stuck) sooner. A better stopping criterion than the one used. Empty string if the exit condition used was already correct.

tags.description: Free-form kebab-case keywords for cross-task retrieval. 3-8 tags. These index orthogonally to task_type (e.g. 'race-condition', 'pytest', 'monorepo').

confidence.description: How reliable and generalizable this finding is, from 0 to 1. Findings below 0.5 are not written to the store — they are too speculative or too session-specific to help anyone else.

timestamp.description: UTC creation time in ISO 8601 (RFC 3339) format.

source.description: Provenance of the finding. Optional but recommended. Implementations may add fields here without breaking the protocol.

agent.description: Identifier of the agent/tool that produced the finding.

session_id.description: Opaque id of the session the finding was distilled from.

cwd.description: Working directory of the originating task. Useful for local debugging; strip before publishing if it leaks paths.
